10.heading: the Lord:
refs: We have not abandoned the Lord
and we still serve him according to His own law. But what Abijah urged concerning the state of religion in Judah was not strictly just
and, as spoken by him, it favoured ostentation. Abijah himself was but an indifferent character
and idolatry was evidently connived at in his days. Yet it was true, that the men of Judah had the priests, ordinances, and worship of Jehovah among them
that there were numbers of pious worshippers in the land
that theirs was the more righteous cause
that Jehovah was on their side as their Captain, while Israel fought against him
and that the presence of the priests with the sacred trumpets was a token of His presence and favour. 2Ch 11:16-17
10.body:
We have not abandoned the Lord; and we still serve him according to His own law. But what Abijah urged concerning the state of religion in Judah was not strictly just; and, as spoken by him, it favoured ostentation. Abijah himself was but an indifferent character; and idolatry was evidently connived at in his days. Yet it was true, that the men of Judah had the priests, ordinances, and worship of Jehovah among them; that there were numbers of pious worshippers in the land; that theirs was the more righteous cause; that Jehovah was on their side as their Captain, while Israel fought against him; and that the presence of the priests with the sacred trumpets was a token of His presence and favour. 2Ch 11:16-17
